      <h1>Decision Rights and Gate Matrix: Who Decides What, With Which Evidence</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">An adapted, org-specific decision-rights and approval-gate matrix — the RACI of agent-assisted delivery — ready to post next to the readiness assessment.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-05-decision-rights-gate-matrix</b><br>
      Pack F - People and operating model<br>
      fill order <b>4</b> &middot; type <b>matrix</b><br>
      audience <b>eng-leader</b> &middot; sheet 1 of 3
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-source">
    Source: <b>Governance for AI-Assisted Delivery</b>, <i>The Architecture Decision Matrix</i> &middot;
    <code>handbook/ch05-governance-for-ai-assisted-delivery.qmd</code> L295-323 &middot;
    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch05-governance-for-ai-assisted-delivery.html#sec-governance-decision-matrix">#sec-governance-decision-matrix</a>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    Use the completed WS-05-governance-readiness-assessment and WS-06-role-map-and-staffing-triggers. Start with the seven book rows and add decision classes that recur in your pull-request reviews or incident postmortems. Name what your agent and people actually do, the individual approver, each evidence artifact and its storage location, and the gate as configured today. Reconcile approver names with the role map. Check columns 12 and 16 against the live configuration. Where a gate is not fully in place, name its owner and build-by date. Record the specific irreversible step and whether the agent can write past it.
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    Complete Block B for every agent role you intend to run, including any role you add. Use explicit tool names, exact file scope, and named operations that must stop for human approval — never a wildcard. Complete Block C for the pilot before the steady-state matrix is in force. Then check every column 16, record every yes and its remediation owner below, and sign only after the check is complete.
  </div>

          <td class="fill"><span class="f-owner"></span></td><td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-owner"></span></td><td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
    <p style="font-size:7.4pt;margin:1mm 0 0;color:#454f59">A <code>tools: ["*"]</code> entry is the chapter's named anti-pattern. Do not use wildcards in column 18.</p>
  </div>

        <tr><td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">Philosophy and strategy</span><span class="opt">Architecture</span><span class="opt">Tool selection</span><span class="opt">Implementation</span><span class="opt">Refinement</span></div></td><td class="fill"><span class="f-owner"></span></td><td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td><td class="fill"><span class="f-box"></span></td><td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">yes</span><span class="opt">no</span></div></td></tr>

    <p style="font-size:7.4pt;margin:1mm 0 0;color:#454f59">The agent surfaces options and trade-offs before the call, not as a justification after it.</p>
